summary: A rare 1930 'Grange Hall' type log lookout on the Lolo National Forest, staffed until 1972, restored by volunteers in 2017 and rentable today.

facts.design: Grange Hall type ground cab: 14x14 ft, four courses of large logs on a short talus/stone foundation; predates the standard L-4 design

access.note: No vehicle access; reached by a 3-mile trail. Open by reservation for rental June to early October.

visit.trail_note: 3 miles one way from the Big Hole Trailhead, open to hikers, horses and mountain bikes; roughly a 60-90 minute drive from Plains, MT to the trailhead

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lolo National Forest, Plains/Thompson Falls Ranger District

events.note: Built for the Cabinet National Forest (now part of the Lolo National Forest)
Last staffed as a fire lookout; abandoned after fire detection moved away from fixed lookouts
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register April 24, 2009, nominated by Gary Weber
Restoration completed through a series of Passport in Time volunteer projects
First year open to the public for overnight rental via Recreation.gov

corrections.proposed: Grange Hall type ground cab (14x14 ft log structure on a talus foundation)
corrections.evidence: Both the Recreation.gov listing and the Forest Service's Lolo National Forest page describe it as a rare 'Grange Hall' type lookout predating the L-4 design, one of only two such intact examples on the Lolo National Forest.

sources.title: Big Hole Lookout
sources.publisher: Lolo National Forest, USDA Forest Service

notes_for_editor: No newspaper or NRHP nomination form located; the 1984 date is NRHP-eligibility, not a formal National Register listing, and the story is careful to say so. Two official-ish sources (Recreation.gov listing vs. the Forest Service's own Lolo NF page) disagree slightly on the lookout's water source: non-potable spring 3/4 mile downhill vs. a filterable spring 0.5 mile away. Wikipedia's 'Big Hole Lookout' article was used only to find the underlying USFS citation (fs.usda.gov/r01/lolo/recreation/big-hole-lookout), not cited directly, per the guide. Record's existing 'design' field was null; proposed a correction above. One WebSearch call used, plus WebFetch on two known URLs. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): firelookout.com actually lists the elevation as 6919 ft, not 6,922 ft, so that figure is now cited to NHLR alone; the 'Cabinet National Forest' detail and the precise staffed-to-1972 date are not on firelookout.com or NHLR's visible text respectively and were re-cited to the sources that actually state them (Recreation.gov and the USFS Lolo NF page); a missing footnote on the cabin's furnishings/vault-toilet sentence was added.
